analysis.investment_thesis: Helloji Holidays is a sub-₹40 Cr micro-cap travel agency with a near-zero 0.51% ROE and a P/E of 18.8x that implies no margin of safety whatsoever against such feeble profitability. There is no visible growth story, no niche dominance, and no PEG math that works — this is a pass.
key_strengths: High promoter holding of 69.97% indicates skin in the game
Travel/tourism sector has structural Indian tailwinds post-COVID
Surprising DII (8.40%) + FII (5.81%) presence for a ₹39 Cr float
key_risks: ROE of 0.51% is effectively no earnings power — P/E 18.8 is unjustified
Commoditized tour-package business with zero moat vs MakeMyTrip/Thomas Cook/local agents
₹39.4 Cr market cap + BSE-only = illiquid, prone to promoter-driven price action
red_flags: P/E 18.8x on negligible earnings = PEG undefined/absurd
Recent SME-style listing with no demonstrated growth trajectory in data provided
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Lynch checklist fails on nearly every line. I want fast growers with 20%+ earnings growth at PEG under 1.0; here I have a 0.51% ROE which tells me the business barely earns its cost of capital, let alone compounds it. At an 18.8x P/E on trivial earnings, I'm paying a growth multiple for a company showing no growth evidence in the snapshot. Tour operators are a tough, fragmented, low-margin business where aggregators (MakeMyTrip, Yatra, EaseMyTrip) and nimble Instagram-era DMCs both squeeze the middle — a ₹39 Cr player has no pricing power or scale advantage to exploit.

The only mildly interesting flag is the institutional presence (FII 5.81% + DII 8.40%) in such a tiny float, which is unusual and warrants a "what do they know" question — but in micro-cap travel, this often reflects anchor/IPO allocation rather than conviction. Until I see revenue growth of 25%+, ROE climbing above 15%, and a clear niche (e.g., a dominant corporate-travel vertical or a signature destination specialty), there's no story here. Pass, and revisit only if earnings inflect hard for 2-3 consecutive quarters.
